messages:
Jordan L.: Hey folks 999999999999Got a case: employee saw an in-network retina specialist but insurer denied as OON. EOB says "provider not contracted" but the provider listed on the EOB is the hospital tax ID, not the physician NPI. Any quick playbook?
Renee M.: Common. Hospital sometimes bills under facility TIN which can trigger OON if the facility isn't in-network for that CPT. Ask provider to rebill under the physician's NPI/TIN and resubmit as professional claim.
Tom B.: While we wait, request an itemized bill and the physician's billing NPI. If they rebill, insurer usually reprocesses within 14-30 days.
Jordan L.: Employee is worried about balance billing. What do we tell them for now?
Liz K.: Send them a short "coverage pending" note and proof of active enrollment. Use benefits portal digital ID and our temporary coverage letter. Also advise them to save all bills and EOBs.
benefits-bot: Automated: For balance-billing protection, reference state surprise billing laws and federal No Surprises Act. If the service was emergency or ancillary, member protections may apply. Typical reprocessing window: 14-45 days.
Renee M.: Template to provider billing (paste into email):```Hello, Please re-submit the claim for [MemberName], DOS [MM/DD/YYYY] under the physician's professional NPI/TIN (NPI: [#######], TIN: [#######]) and indicate resubmission as "Corrected/Adjusted Claim". Original claim #: [orig_claim]. Attached: member EOB and itemized bill. Please confirm resubmission number and estimated processing time. Thank you, People Ops - benefits@redwood.com```
Tom B.: Insurer appeal template for the employee to file if provider won't rebill:```To: appeals@[insurer].com Subject: Appeal - Reconsideration requested for denied claim [claim#] Member: [Name], DOB [MM/DD/YYYY] We request reconsideration of this claim. The denial references billing under the facility TIN. The service was rendered by an in-network physician (NPI: [#####]). Attached: itemized bill, physician NPI, EOB, and clinical note. Please reprocess under the physician's professional claim. Contact: benefits@redwood.com```
Jordan L.: I'll send both templates to the provider and the employee. Any escalation path if insurer refuses?
Renee M.: If insurer denies reprocessing, open a broker escalation and we can file a formal appeal with supporting docs. If it looks like balance billing, we can submit an external review request via the state's department of insurance.
Liz K.: I've queued a temporary coverage letter for the employee and added case to our tracker (case #BEN-2026-347). Forward any provider receipts and I'll attach them.
Jordan L.: Provider emailed back: they can rebill but need the physician NPI and a copy of the EOB. Sent both. Will update once resub ID comes through. :white_check_mark:
Tom B.: Great. Tell employee to monitor EOB and if they get a bill, don't pay until reprocessing completes. If a collection notice arrives, escalate to People Ops billing support.
Jordan L.: Thanks team, will follow up here. :thumbsup:
